aboutText: Hi my name is Sam Kettlewell-Sites. I am a 27 year old software engineer based in the D.C area and grew up in Richmond VA. I attended James Madison University from 2016-2021 where I graduated with a major in Integrated Science and Technology (ISAT) and a minor in Computer Science. In college I found my joy for programming and continued that on to my professional career. Outside of work I enjoy swimming competitively both on my masters swim team which I help run (Club Tribe) as well as some larger USA swimming compations like TYR pro series meets.
homePage: I am a GovCon software developer based out of Arlington VA. I have been living and working in Arlington since graduating college from James Madison university in 2021. My primary work experience is developer backed, full stack and database development.
growingUp: I was born and raised for my whole childhood in Richmond Va. Richmond provided me a great balance between the energy and unique culture of a city while also never feeling too overwhelmed and still close to nature. One of the most recognizable elements of the City is the river and living just a 5 minute walk from it allowed me to experience the river in all 4 seasons.
swim: Throughout my whole life I have been a competitive swimmer. I started off doing summer league when I was 5 and swam all 14 years for that team. Summer league is where I found my true joy in swimming. Throughout middle school and highschool I swam on a competitive year round team and for my highschool team. In college I joined JMU club swimming which I eventually became the president of. I continue to swim as a masters swimmer for Club Tribe and enjoy the routine of practices and getting to travel the country for swim meets with my friends.
college: I attended James Madison University from 2016 - 2021 where I graduated with a major in ISAT and a minor in computer science.James Madison provided me with the perfect mix of large school in a beautiful environment. Nestled in the Shenandoah valley we were treated to beautiful scenery and easy access to the blue Ridge mountains While in school swam for the club team all 5 years serving as secretary, Vice President and President of the team.
adult: After college I moved to Arlington Virginia to start work as a software engineer. My job is fully remote but my company is based out of Northern Virginia and many of my friends moved to the area after college. One of my favorite parts about the area is the proximity to DC and all the great culture and food. A 15 minute walk and you're in Georgetown enjoying incredible neighborhoods and food, a quick Metro ride and you're watching a Nats game. This area might not be my forever home but for now I am really enjoying it.
hobbies: Outside of swimming I have a few other hobbies. In the winter I like to go snowboarding. Unfortunately we don’t have a lot of big mountains around and the winters on the east coast can be warm and icy but it's still fun. In the summer I like to golf. A favorite activity is hitting a few range balls on a summer evening at East Potomac golf course. It’s wonderful when you have a nice breeze coming off the potomac with the sun setting and planes landing at Regan. Besides that I enjoy working on personal coding projects and the typical video games/ Youtube sesh.

startJob.summary: In August 2021 I started ast a T1 software Enginner at CACI on the FMBT (Financial Management Business Transformation Program) team. The goal of this project is to assist the VA (Veterians Affairs) with converting their legacy accounting system to the modern Momentem system. This involves converting legacy data to fit into the new system, defining new online pathways and systems for accounting documents and transactions to flow between the VA and vendors, as well as assisting the VA with this translation.

conversionTeam.summary: yOn the FMBT team we strived to convert legacy and current accounting data VA systems to a form that can be put into the new accounting system. To do this we used PL/SQL to cross walk the legacy data. To make the process more efficient we used Jenkins jobs with bash scripts to automate converting the constant flow of new transactions.

interfaceTeam.summary: The Interface team's goal is to create services that can receive customers accounting information, transform and insert the data into the Momentum accounting service and return any faulty accounting data to the customers for them to fix. While on the team I got experience with Java development creating proxy services that used soap xml calls to receive data. I also spent time developing SQL extract services that would pull data from the last 24 hours based on predefined requirements, create a txt file out of this data and pass it along to our customers. To deploy these services I got to work with using Red Hats Open Shift service.

automationTeam.summary: The Automation team serves to create efficient solutions for the CACI FMBT team. While on the team I have mostly worked on PySel a Python application that uses Selenium to Automate testing in the Momentum accounting system. Our PySel application reads JSON tests to run and read SQL, and implement custom actions we developed. Such as clicking elements and checking values in a web browser, importing other tests, executing custom JavaScript and many more. When I first started it was a small team of about 3 developers two of which left shortly after starting. Over the Summer of 2023 I led a team of me and two interns as well as an analyst to turn PySel into a strong proof of concept. We developed many test actions for users, developed a reporting system that would give step by step results of the test in HTML and developed a GUI to allow users to update settings, run tests and look at results all from one interface. After the interns left more developers joined the team and we continued to refine PySel and our processes expanding the features that PySel has. We developed Jenkins pipelines to regression test our work and automate deploying releases. The summer of 2024 we converted the PySel GUI over to React. This provided us more flexibility with design, a reactive user interface and a faster GUI experience. To allow PySel to run with the new frontend we developed a flask backend so the front end could make API calls to PySel. Currently we continue to develop PySel and its features as well as explore other technologies like Power BI and Power Automate to create more efficiencies for our entire project.

promoted.summary: I was promoted to T-2 or Technical-2 which is the 2nd level of the CACI engineering track. This promotion came right after my 3rd year at CACI and 3 years in the workforce. This was a good sign as it was the minimum amount of time I could work before being promoted to the next level as CACI requires 3 years of working experience to be promoted. To be promoted to T-2 I needed to demonstrate a strong grasp of technical skills, the ability to problem solve and work without assistance and some leadership on teams.

interns.summary: Over the 3 summers I worked with interns so far I have learned a lot. Both about how to work and guide others and what areas I can improve myself. The first year I had only 1 intern working for me. That was the first time I worked with someone who had less experience then me. It gave me a lot of practice with walking someone through onboarding and helping them through a lot of the same issues I had encountered when I came on. Year two I had two interns working for me and a lot more experience on the team. I was able to work with the interns to develop goals for the summer for them. I assisted them with their work while still letting them take charge in the learning and production of work. I better learned how to delegate out work and had a good enough understanding of the project over all to find the appropriate amount of work for them to tackle. Year 3 was a lot of fun because I had 3 interns working with me who where all returning. This allowed me to better plan out a custom project for them to develop and work on over the summer which would be very beneficial to the project. I served much more as a guiding role giving them the authority to make their own decisions while still serving as a resource and providing guidance making sure their work was still inline with the teams goals. This gave them the confidence to develop a really cool project that they could present and be very proud of at the end of the summer.

brit.summary: The BRIT project was my first time being the sole developer on a project. The goal was to create views inside of  Azure Synapse to allow the BRIT to see detailed line by line and summary rolled up accounting lines and transactions based on filtering criteria like organization type. This project really pushed me to work on my communication skills with clients. I worked with the clients to discuss what their needs were, properly demonstrate what we could develop for them with the tools we planned to use and work with my business analyst on creating deliverables of what would be produced. After about 6 months of requirements gathering and another 6 weeks of development I was able to deliver a product that satisfied all the needs of the client.

personalWebsite.desc: A personal website about myself that is used to both allow others to learn more about me and practice my Dynamic website development skills.

ncaaRanking.desc: A small data science project using Python to determine all time rankings for NCAA swim teams. To do this historical data was scraped from NCAA archives and data was accumulated to show teams all time rankings.
